description: Erection of an additional storey to create one additional self-contained residential unit (Use Class C3).
decision_conditions: <p>The proposed development would result in a substandard form of development for future occupiers due to the failure to provide private outdoor amenity space (such as a balcony or terrace) for a family unit. The omission of dedicated private amenity space would harm the living conditions, health, and well-being of future occupants, contrary to policy D6 (Housing quality and standards) of the London Plan (2021), policies LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character), and LP17 (Housing Design) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020), and the Mayor of London's Housing Design Standards SPD (2023).</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of its size, scale, bulk, massing and detailed design would result in an obtrusive, unsympathetic and incompatible form of development which disrupts the established grain of development in the area that would harm the visual amenities of the host building&nbsp; and the surrounding streetscape. As such, the proposed development is considered contrary to policies D3 (Optimising site capacity through the design-led approach) and D4 (Delivering good design) of the London Plan (2021) and policies LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character) and LP17 (Housing Design) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020) and Hackney's Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD (2025).&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of the failure to submit an Overheating Risk Assessment to demonstrate that the unit would provide adequate thermal comfort, risks overheating without justification or passive shading. The proposal is contrary to policy SI 4 (Managing heat risk) of the London Plan (2021) and policy LP54 (Overheating) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of the lack of provision of affordable housing, would fail to adequately contribute towards the provision of mixed and balanced communities and housing need in the local area. As such, the development would be contrary to policy H4 (Delivering affordable housing) and policy H5 (Threshold approach to applications) of the London Plan (2021), policy LP12 (Meeting Housing Needs) and policy LP13 (Affordable Housing) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020), Paragraph 64 of the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF 2024), and the guidance contained within the Hackney Planning Contributions SPD (2020).</p>

<p>In the absence of a suitable legal undertaking (Section 106 agreement) to secure that the occupiers of the new residential unit would be ineligible to apply for on-street parking permits within the Controlled Parking Zone (CPZ), the proposal would result in increased parking stress on the local highway network. Consequently, the development would have an adverse impact on local parking conditions, highway safety, and the promotion of sustainable modes of transport, contrary to policy T1 (Strategic approach to transport) and policy T4 (Assessing and mitigating transport impacts) of the London Plan (2021), and policies LP43 (Transport and Development) and LP45 (Parking and Car Free Development) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of a lack of sufficient energy efficiency measures and/or a legal agreement to secure a financial contribution towards off-site carbon offsetting, would fail to achieve the required reductions in carbon dioxide emissions. The proposal is therefore contrary to policies SI 2 (Minimising Greenhouse Gas Emissions) and SI 4 (Managing heat risk)&nbsp;of the London Plan (2021), policies LP54 (Overheating and Adapting to Climate Change) and LP55 (Mitigating Climate Change) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020), and the guidance contained within the Hackney Sustainable Design and Construction SPD (2016).</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of failure to provide information regarding the siting, specification, and noise outputs for the proposed Air Source Heat Pump (ASHP), fails to demonstrate that the equipment would not generate unacceptable levels of noise and vibration. The proposal risks causing undue noise disturbance to the detriment of the residential amenities of neighbouring occupiers, contrary to policy D14 (Noise) of the London Plan (2021) and policies LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character) and LP2 (Development and Amenity) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).</p>

<p><span data-sheets-root="1" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial;">The proposed development fails to demonstrate that sufficient, safe, and conveniently accessible cycle parking can be accommodated on-site. Due to the absence of detailed plans, the proposal fails to verify that adequate space and manoeuvrability can be provided to ensure secure and weatherproof cycle storage for future occupiers. Consequently, the scheme fails to encourage active travel and sustainable transport modes, contrary to policy T5 (Cycling) of the London Plan (2021), policies LP41 (Controlling Highway and Transport Impacts), LP42 (Walking and Cycling), LP43 (Transport and Development), and LP45 (Parking and Car Free Development) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020), and Hackney’s Sustainable Transport SPD.</span></p>

<p>The proposed development fails to demonstrate that adequate and conveniently accessible refuse and recycling storage can be provided on-site. Due to the absence of detailed plans showing an appropriate location, capacity, and access route, the scheme fails to ensure a safe, secure, and accessible passage for future occupiers or to satisfy operational collection requirements for refuse operatives. Consequently, the proposal fails to demonstrate satisfactory waste management, contrary to policy D6 (Housing Quality and Standards) and policy SI 7 (Reducing Waste and Supporting the Circular Economy) of the London Plan (2021), and policies LP1 (<span style="background-color: transparent; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 11pt; white-space: pre-wrap; text-align: justify;">Design Quality and Local Character) and </span>LP57 (Waste) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).</p>
